prompt: Split the REPL `line` into `cmd` (first word, lowercased) and `rest` (everything after the whitespace that follows it, inner spacing kept verbatim, outer whitespace stripped). Missing parts are ''.
given: line = "  RUN phi3   tell me  a joke  "
check:
assert (cmd, rest) == ("run", "phi3   tell me  a joke"), (cmd, rest)
rerun(line="load    phi")
assert (cmd, rest) == ("load", "phi"), f"{(cmd, rest)}: split() with no separator skips the whole whitespace run"
rerun(line="list")
assert (cmd, rest) == ("list", ""), (cmd, rest)
rerun(line="   ")
assert (cmd, rest) == ("", ""), "a blank line must not crash: pad the split before unpacking"
why: split(maxsplit=1) with NO separator skips the whitespace run and keeps the rest verbatim; shlex would eat the spacing.

prompt: Set `name` to the entry of `names` matching `typed`, case-insensitively: an exact match wins, else a unique prefix match. No match: raise provider.UnknownModel(f"no model matches {typed!r}"). Several: provider.UnknownModel(f"{typed!r} is ambiguous: a, b") with the candidates sorted.
answer:
want = typed.casefold()
matches = [n for n in names if n.casefold() == want] or sorted(n for n in names if n.casefold().startswith(want))
if not matches:
    raise provider.UnknownModel(f"no model matches {typed!r}")
if len(matches) > 1:
    raise provider.UnknownModel(f"{typed!r} is ambiguous: {', '.join(matches)}")
name = matches[0]
why: Exact match first, then the prefix list: 0 = unknown, 2+ = ambiguous; raise the provider's own namespaced error.

prompt: Write the handler `cmd_load(rest, out)`: blank rest raises UsageError("load <model>"); otherwise resolve the name against CLIENT.list_models(), CLIENT.load it, and print `loaded <name> (<load_ms> ms)` from the dict load returns. resolve_model(typed, models) is provided.
why: Handlers are (rest, out), print with file=out, go through CLIENT, and RAISE; read the shape load() returns.

prompt: Build `COMMANDS` mapping 'list' and 'load' to (handler, help text) tuples. Then define `dispatch(line, out) -> bool`: parse it, call the handler with (rest, out); if the handler raises anything, print `TypeName: message` to out and return False. (Assume the command is known.)
given:
import io
# provided: parse_line(line) -> (cmd, rest), cmd_list(rest, out), cmd_load(rest, out)
check:
assert isinstance(COMMANDS.get("list"), tuple) and COMMANDS["list"][0] is cmd_list, "COMMANDS['list'] should be the tuple (cmd_list, help_text)"
assert COMMANDS["load"][0] is cmd_load and isinstance(COMMANDS["load"][1], str), COMMANDS.get("load")
_o = io.StringIO()
assert dispatch("load phi", _o) is True, _o.getvalue()
assert _o.getvalue() == "loaded phi3:mini (230 ms)\n", f"{_o.getvalue()!r}: call it, entry[0](rest, out)"
_o = io.StringIO()
assert dispatch("load gpt4", _o) is False, "an error should return False"
assert _o.getvalue() == "UnknownModel: no model matches 'gpt4'\n", f"{_o.getvalue()!r}: print f\"{{type(e).__name__}}: {{e}}\""
_o = io.StringIO()
assert dispatch("load", _o) is False and _o.getvalue() == "UsageError: load <model>\n", repr(_o.getvalue())
why: Dict of (handler, help) TUPLES; entry[0](rest, out) calls it; the one catch-all prints f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}".

prompt: Write `repl(stdin, out)`: for each line of stdin (no prompt needed), strip it; stop on exit/quit in any case; skip blank lines; otherwise dispatch(line, out). Print 'bye' to out at the end (on exit or EOF). dispatch is provided.
given:
import io
stdin = io.StringIO("list

   load phi  
EXIT
list
")
check:
_o = io.StringIO()
repl(stdin, _o)
assert _seen == ["list", "load phi"], f"dispatched {_seen}: strip, skip blanks, stop at exit/quit (any case)"
assert _o.getvalue().endswith("bye\n"), f"{_o.getvalue()!r}: print('bye', file=out)"
_seen.clear()
_o = io.StringIO()
repl(io.StringIO("quit\n"), _o)
assert _seen == [] and _o.getvalue().endswith("bye\n"), (_seen, _o.getvalue())
_o = io.StringIO()
repl(io.StringIO("list"), _o)
assert _seen == ["list"] and _o.getvalue().endswith("bye\n"), "EOF without exit should still end with bye"
why: `for line in stdin:` ends at EOF; strip first, then check exit/quit with .lower() and skip blanks.

prompt: Set `result = CLIENT.run(name, prompt)`, but if the model isn't loaded (the provider raises its NotLoaded error), print `(auto-loading <name>)` to out, load it, and run again.
given:
import io
CLIENT = provider   # nothing is loaded yet
name, prompt = "phi3:mini", "tell me  a joke"
out = io.StringIO()
check:
assert result["text"] == "phi3:mini says: tell me  a joke", result
assert out.getvalue() == "(auto-loading phi3:mini)\n", repr(out.getvalue())
assert provider.state["loaded"] == "phi3:mini"
assert provider.count("run") == 2 and provider.count("load") == 1, provider.state["calls"]
out = io.StringIO()
rerun()
assert out.getvalue() == "", "already loaded: no auto-load line"
why: Lean on the provider's error: `except provider.NotLoaded:` (namespaced, from `import provider`), load, retry once.

prompt: Print each benchmark round to out in ROUND order as `round N: <ms> ms, <tokens> tokens`, then `min <ms> ms | avg <ms:.1f> ms | <tok/s:.1f> tok/s` (tok/s = total tokens / total seconds).
given:
import io
out = io.StringIO()
results = [  # completion order, as the provider returns them
    {"round": 2, "ms": 115, "tokens": 64},
    {"round": 1, "ms": 145, "tokens": 64},
    {"round": 3, "ms": 160, "tokens": 64},
]
answer:
for r in sorted(results, key=lambda r: r["round"]):
    print(f"round {r['round']}: {r['ms']} ms, {r['tokens']} tokens", file=out)
times = [r["ms"] for r in results]
tok_s = sum(r["tokens"] for r in results) / (sum(times) / 1000)
print(f"min {min(times)} ms | avg {sum(times) / len(times):.1f} ms | {tok_s:.1f} tok/s", file=out)
check:
_want = ("round 1: 145 ms, 64 tokens
round 2: 115 ms, 64 tokens
round 3: 160 ms, 64 tokens
"
         "min 115 ms | avg 140.0 ms | 457.1 tok/s
")
assert out.getvalue() == _want, f"{out.getvalue()!r}: rounds must print in r['round'] order"
why: sorted(results, key=lambda r: r['round']): use the provider's field, not your loop index or list order.

prompt: Write `class ProviderClient`: `self.calls` is a Counter; `_call(fn, *args)` counts fn.__name__ and returns fn(*args); `run(name, prompt)` goes through _call with provider.run.
check:
_c = ProviderClient()
provider.load("phi3:mini")
_r = _c.run("phi3:mini", "hi")
assert _r["text"] == "phi3:mini says: hi", _r
assert _c._call(provider.loaded) == "phi3:mini", "_call must return fn(*args)"
assert _c.calls == {"run": 1, "loaded": 1}, f"{dict(_c.calls)}: count fn.__name__ in _call"
assert provider.count("run") == 1, "run should hit the provider exactly once"
why: One chokepoint: every method is `return self._call(provider.x, *args)`, so retry/caching later override one place.

prompt: Write `call_with_retry(fn, *args)`: up to `attempts` calls, retrying ONLY the provider's transient Timeout, sleeping base_delay * 2**i between attempts (none after the last), and re-raising the final Timeout. Any other error propagates at once.
given:
attempts, base_delay = 3, 0.1
slept = []
sleep = slept.append   # injected: records instead of waiting
check:
provider.load("phi3:mini")
provider.state["fail"] = 2
_r = call_with_retry(provider.run, "phi3:mini", "hi")
assert _r["text"] == "phi3:mini says: hi", _r
assert slept == [0.1, 0.2], f"{slept}: want backoff 0.1, 0.2"
assert provider.count("run") == 3, provider.count("run")
slept.clear(); provider.state["calls"].clear(); provider.state["fail"] = 5
try:
    call_with_retry(provider.run, "phi3:mini", "hi")
except provider.Timeout:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("after the last attempt, re-raise the Timeout")
assert slept == [0.1, 0.2], f"{slept}: no sleep after the final attempt"
assert provider.count("run") == 3, f"{provider.count('run')} calls, want exactly attempts=3"
slept.clear(); provider.state["calls"].clear(); provider.state["fail"] = 0
try:
    call_with_retry(provider.run, "nope", "hi")
except provider.UnknownModel:
    pass
assert provider.count("run") == 1, f"UnknownModel was retried ({provider.count('run')} calls): catch provider.Timeout only"
assert slept == [], slept
why: Retry ONLY the transient error (`except provider.Timeout:`); bare `raise` on the last attempt; never retry 'doesn't exist'.

prompt: Write `list_models()` with a TTL cache in `cache` ({'value': models, 'at': time}): return the cached value if it's younger than ttl (age < ttl), else fetch provider.list_models() and store it with clock(). If the fetch raises provider.Timeout and a cached copy exists, return the stale copy; with no copy, let it raise.
given:
now = [0.0]
clock = lambda: now[0]   # injected so the test controls time
ttl = 30.0
cache = {}
check:
_a, _b = list_models(), list_models()
assert _a == _b == provider.MODELS, _a
assert provider.count("list_models") == 1, "second call within ttl should come from the cache"
now[0] = 29.9
list_models()
assert provider.count("list_models") == 1, "29.9s old is still fresh"
now[0] = 30.0
list_models()
assert provider.count("list_models") == 2, "exactly ttl old is stale: compare age < ttl"
now[0] = 100.0
provider.state["fail"] = 1
try:
    assert list_models() == provider.MODELS
except provider.Timeout:
    raise AssertionError("stale-on-error: return the old cached copy when the refresh times out") from None
cache.clear()
provider.state["fail"] = 1
try:
    list_models()
except provider.Timeout:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("no cached copy: the Timeout should propagate")
why: Store (value, stored_at) from an injected clock; fresh if now - at < ttl; on Timeout serve stale, else re-raise.

prompt: Write `main(argv, stdin, out, client=None) -> int`: if client is given, install it as the module-level CLIENT. No argv: run repl(stdin, out) and return 0. Otherwise dispatch the argv words joined by spaces; return 0 on success, 1 on failure.
given:
import io
CLIENT = provider
# provided: repl(stdin, out), dispatch(line, out) -> bool
check:
_o = io.StringIO()
assert main(["run", "phi", "hello"], io.StringIO(), _o) == 0
assert _log == [("dispatch", "run phi hello")], _log
assert main(["bogus"], io.StringIO(), _o) == 1, "a failed dispatch should exit 1"
_log.clear()
assert main([], io.StringIO("list\n"), _o) == 0
assert _log == [("repl", "list\n")], f"{_log}: no argv -> repl(stdin, out)"
_new = object()
main([], io.StringIO(""), _o, client=_new)
assert CLIENT is _new, "CLIENT wasn't rebound: rebinding a module name inside a function needs `global CLIENT`"
main([], io.StringIO(""), _o)
assert CLIENT is _new, "client=None must leave CLIENT alone"
why: `global CLIENT` to REBIND a module name in a function; argv mode is " ".join(argv) through the same dispatch.

prompt: Rank every name: append (bench(name), name) to `ranked`, or if it raises a provider error, append "<name> (<ErrorType>)" to `failed` and keep going. Whatever model was loaded before must be loaded again afterwards, even if something unexpected blows up.
given:
CLIENT = provider   # a model is already loaded
names = ["phi3:mini", "mistral:7b", "gemma2:2b"]
ranked, failed = [], []
# bench(name) is provided: loads the model, returns its avg ms; may raise any provider.ProviderError
why: Per-item try/except provider.ProviderError degrades instead of aborting; the outer try/finally restores the session.
